do.name: Medieval Week
do.detail: For a week in early August the town dresses up: jousting, markets, taverns and hundreds of events staged among the church ruins.

do.name: Cycle out from the walls
do.detail: Gotland is flat and laced with quiet lanes and marked bike paths, so a day ride along the coast needs no training and no hills.

do.name: Follow the ring wall
do.detail: Around three and a half kilometres of 13th century wall still stand, studded with towers and gates, and walking the outside costs nothing.

do.name: Roofless church ruins in the old town
do.detail: A fire in 1525 left a dozen churches open to the sky. S:ta Karin on the main square and St Nicolai are the ones to seek out.

do.name: Beaches and raukar sea stacks
do.detail: Sand at Tofta and Sudersand for swimming, and weathered limestone pillars standing offshore on the northern coast and Faro.

do.name: Gotlands Museum and its guided city walks
do.detail: Fornsalen holds the island's Viking and Hanseatic finds, and the same museum runs walking tours of the ruins it looks after.

do.name: Island specialities: saffron pancake and truffle
do.detail: Saffron rice pancake with cream and jam is the island dessert. Lamb, asparagus and autumn truffles fill the farm shops and markets.
